subject: Acceptance storyline, exit criteria and test checks for MedNota evaluation
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@mednota.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acceptance storyline, exit criteria and test checks for MedNota evaluation

Liam —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I put together a concise acceptance "storyline" to make the evaluation deterministic for both sides. The goal: by the end of the 4-week pilot we have objective pass/fail signals and a short list of evidence that will clear procurement to move to a paid Dedicated contract.

High-level proposal (attached MAP-draft.xlsx):
- Week 0: Environment & data onboarding (sample dataset, API keys, KMS config) — success = ingestion < 24h and sample inference within SLA
- Week 1: Core accuracy & safety smoke tests — success = >= 92% on prioritized test prompts and zero high-severity safety hits
- Week 2: Throughput and latency verification (production-like traffic profiles) — success = median token latency < 120ms and sustained throughput for 15m bursts
- Week 3: Regression & edge-case sweep + security evidence review — success = no critical regressions vs baseline + requested artifacts for compliance (audit logs, config snapshots)
- Week 4: Signoff window & procurement checklist (DocuSign link + contract redlines) — success = mutual signoff + purchase order commitment date

Acceptance tests (summary in acceptance-tests.md):
- Functional: 8 canonical prompts + 6 negative-safety probes (pass/fail matrix)
- Performance: 3 traffic patterns, warm/cold cache runs, KV cache hit verification
- Reliability: 48-hour soak run with error-rate < 0.5%
- Evidence: sample audit log export, latency heatmap, and model version hash

Questions for you (short):
1) Are the weeks above aligned with MedNota's availability to ingest a redacted dataset?
2) Any additional compliance artifacts your procurement team requires beyond SOC2 scope & audit logs?
3) Preferred signoff approver (title/email) so we can add to the MAP?

Attached: MAP-draft.xlsx (milestones & owners), acceptance-tests.md (test cases), mednota-evidence.zip (example artifact layout).

If that looks good I'll circulate a one-sheet MAP with owners and dates and schedule the kickoff for next Monday.

Thanks —
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@mednota.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance storyline, exit criteria and test checks for MedNota evaluation

Sergio —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. High level this matches our expectations. Quick clarifications:
- We can provide a redacted dataset by Friday (internal privacy team signed off) — so Week 0 looks achievable if we kickoff next Monday.
- Procurement flagged two items they want in the evidence bundle: (a) retention policy for inference logs, and (b) a sample data deletion runbook. Can you confirm where those live in your artifact list?
- Our security lead would like to see how you handle key rotation in the Private deployment path; can you add a short test (rotate keys, validate ongoing sessions) to Week 3?

Also copying our procurement contact (procurement@mednota.com) to keep timelines visible.

On the signoff approver: Emily Ramos, VP Product (emily.ramos@mednota.com) will be the business approver; procurement will issue PO after the evidence bundle.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Integrations, MedNota

Subject: Re: Acceptance storyline, exit criteria and test checks for MedNota evaluation

Liam / Sergio —

Good catch on the retention & key rotation asks. I've updated the acceptance-tests.md to include two discrete verification steps:
1) Retention policy verification: deliverable = policy snippet + automated retention job run (simulate 30-day deletion on sample data) — test passes when deleted items are absent from API queries and the audit log records the operation. Owner: Marissa Cole.
2) Key rotation smoke: rotate service key, verify ongoing in-flight requests succeed (no auth drop), and validate new logs show new key id. Owner: Karthik Iyer.

I added both to Week 3 tasks and bumped the security sweep window to include the key rotation test. I've attached the updated acceptance-tests.md.

Proposed kickoff: Monday 2026-08-17 10:00 PT. Agenda (30m): confirm dataset delivery, map owners to each test, and set the PO target date (we should aim to have PO signed within 7 business days of final signoff).

If that works for MedNota I'll send a calendar invite and publish the MAP to the Drive link Sergio shared.

Cheers,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

All —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Confirming next steps:
- Kickoff Monday 2026-08-17 10:00 PT (calendar invite sent).
- Deliverables: updated MAP in Drive, acceptance-tests.md (v2 attached), artifact-bundle created within 48h of signoff. Owner matrix included in MAP-draft.xlsx.
- Procurement ask on Dedicated pricing: Ben will produce a 1-page cost delta and add to the Drive before the kickoff.
- Signoff approver: Emily Ramos (business) + Procurement PO. DocuSign link will be issued as soon as the artifact bundle and contract draft are uploaded.

Sampling of acceptance exit gates (for visibility):
- Ingestion Gate: sample data ingested and first inference completed within 24h (evidence: ingestion log + sample inference response)
- Safety Gate: prioritized safety probes pass (no high severity)
- Performance Gate: median token latency < 120ms for acceptance traffic pattern
- Compliance Gate: retention and deletion verification completed, audit logs exported

If there are no objections from MedNota at kickoff we'll execute the MAP as-is. Ben — please note the PO target (7 business days post-signoff) and prepare a one-pager.

I'll keep the thread for updates during the pilot.

Sergio
